prompts.source: CREATE A NEW COPYRIGHT-SAFE, ANATOMY-LED EDUCATIONAL PALEOART SCENE. Use reference image 1 only for Triceratops horridus identity, reference 2 only for Edmontosaurus annectens identity, and reference 3 only for Tyrannosaurus rex identity. Do not copy any reference camera, pose, background, lighting, or full composition. VERTICAL 4:5 COMPOSITION, designed for both phone and desktop. This is a cautious hypothetical Hell Creek environmental scene during the early atmospheric disturbance after the Chicxulub impact, NOT the impact moment. Do not show the asteroid, a fireball, crater, explosion, shockwave, tsunami, volcano, lava, wall of fire, or burning animals. The environment is the subject: a vast dim amber-charcoal particulate sky fills about 70 percent of the frame, with diffuse obscured sunlight, fine suspended dust, and gust-bent ferns and conifer branches. Keep the horizon very low, near the bottom quarter. No S-curve river, no opposed banks, no concentric terrain, no misty depth layers, no framing log, no overhead view. EXACTLY THREE DINOSAURS TOTAL, one of each species and no others. All three are fully separated by broad empty ground, at different horizontal positions and slightly different depths, forming a loose broken triangle rather than a lineup or confrontation. No eye contact, no chase, no attack, no family or herd behavior, no blood, no wounds, no carcass. LOWER LEFT: exactly one Triceratops horridus, small in frame, rear three-quarter walking calmly toward the left edge. Preserve a low long four-legged body, exactly four legs, one tail, two long brow horns, one short nasal horn, closed beak, and a solid skull-attached frill without holes or a spike crown. LOWER CENTER FARTHER BACK: exactly one Edmontosaurus annectens, smaller, rear three-quarter walking away on a separate patch. Preserve one long low crestless duck-billed head, a broad closed beak, modest low soft-tissue midline ridge rather than a bony crest or sail, exactly four limbs, and one long tail. LOWER RIGHT: exactly one Tyrannosaurus rex, small-to-medium in frame, rear three-quarter moving toward the right edge without looking at the herbivores. Preserve a deep broad tyrannosaur skull, lips over closed teeth, exactly two strong hind legs, two tiny chest-held arms with exactly two fingers on each readable hand, and one continuous heavy tail. CAMERA AND SPATIAL GRAMMAR: extremely low upward-looking wide camera, skyfield-negative-space composition, the three animals occupy only the bottom 25 to 30 percent and none exceeds 24 percent of frame height. Asymmetric empty sky dominates. Natural museum-grade digital paleoart, restrained non-sensational colors, readable silhouettes, complete bodies inside frame, no text, labels, borders, diagrams, logos, or watermark.
prompts.correction: STRICT LOCAL CONTENT CORRECTION of reference image 1. Preserve its vertical 4:5 canvas, enormous amber-charcoal dusty sky, tiny obscured sun, low horizon, restrained color, ground texture, conifers, low upward camera, skyfield-negative-space composition, and the existing separated Edmontosaurus and Tyrannosaurus positions as closely as possible. REMOVE the entire Triceratops at lower left, including its head, horns, frill, body, all four legs, tail, shadow, and any ghost fragments. Reconstruct that entire lower-left area as empty open Hell Creek floodplain with low ferns, broken twigs, and undisturbed ground consistent with the rest of the scene. Do not replace it with any animal, skull, carcass, track, rock shaped like an animal, or large tree. FINAL EXACT ANIMAL COUNT: TWO DINOSAURS TOTAL AND NO OTHERS. 1) Exactly one Edmontosaurus annectens remains in the lower center-left far midground, clearly separated, rear three-quarter walking calmly toward the left/away. Use reference image 2 only for identity: long low crestless duck-billed head, broad closed beak, modest low soft-tissue midline ridge rather than a bony crest or sail, exactly four limbs, one continuous tail. It must not look back at the predator. 2) Exactly one Tyrannosaurus rex remains in the lower right, rear three-quarter walking calmly toward the right edge. Use reference image 3 only for identity: deep broad tyrannosaur skull, closed lips over teeth, exactly two strong hind legs, exactly two tiny chest-held arms with exactly two fingers on each readable hand, one continuous heavy tail. It must not look at or approach the Edmontosaurus. Keep broad empty ground between both animals. No chase, attack, eye contact, threat posture, herd, family, running, blood, wounds, carcass, asteroid, meteor, fireball, crater, explosion, shockwave, tsunami, volcano, lava, flames, or burning forest. The sky is an educational hypothetical post-impact atmospheric disturbance, not the impact moment. No text, labels, borders, logos, or watermark.

evidence.supportedClaim: Tyrannosaurus and Edmontosaurus belong to the upper Hell Creek fauna, and the Chicxulub impact produced atmospheric dust and other agents capable of strongly reducing sunlight and altering climate.
evidence.claimBoundary: The exact shared location, date, survival interval, sky colour, dust density, visible Sun and animal responses are reconstructed. The scene does not show the impactor or prove that these individuals witnessed, fled, interacted, or survived a specific interval after the impact.
